Ideal

eye-DEE-uhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ideal is perfect for a purpose; the best possible.

The flat, grassy field was an ideal spot for our picnic.

Worked Example

Quiet and full of books, the library is an ideal place to study.

Quiet and full of books is exactly what studying needs. When a place fits a purpose perfectly, it is ideal.

How Ideal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

perfect

perfect: as good as it can possibly be

best

best: better than all the others

Antonyms

imperfect

imperfect: having flaws or problems

unsuitable

unsuitable: not right for the purpose

How Strong Is It? — Suitable → ideal → Perfect

Suitable vs. ideal

Suitable vs. ideal: Suitable is milder: a cloudy day is suitable for a walk, even if it is not perfect.

Perfect vs. ideal

Perfect vs. ideal: Perfect is the strongest: a perfect score means not one single mistake.

Put it together

Put it together: Ide- means a form or pattern, so ideal describes something that matches the perfect pattern of what it should be.
